prs.title: [CI] Reclaim GPU memory between model initialization tests
prs.author: khluu
prs.body_head:
## Summary

Deflake the model-initialization tests in `tests/models/test_initialization.py` by reclaiming GPU memory between tests.

### Flaky tests addressed

From a Buildkite flaky-test analysis (suite `ci-1`):

| Test | Reliability | Failed/Total |
|---|---|---|
| `test_can_initialize_small_subset[InternVLChatModel]` | 0.998 | 8/3288 |

Buildkite: https://buildkite.com/organizations/vllm/analytics/suites/ci-1/tests/b1f1fe69-2515-83bb-bbd3-b15a219bbdce

The same failure mode plausibly affects the sibling tests in this module (`test_can_initialize_large_subset`, e.g. `Step3TextForCausalLM` 5/1072, `Step3VLForConditionalGeneration` 5/1050, `Gemma4MTPModel` 3/1050), which run at the same `gpu_memory_utilization=0.80`.

### Root cause

Each parametrized case in this module builds a full vLLM `LLM` in a fresh subprocess via `create_new_process_for_each_test()` with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.80` — the source itself carries the comment "these tests seem to produce leftover memory". On NVIDIA the subprocess is **forked**, and its VRAM is only reclaimed asynchronously by the driver when the subprocess exits. The next test can start (and allocate ~80% of the GPU, e.g. an 18 GiB H200 MIG slice) before that reclamation completes, so leftover memory from a preceding test OOMs a later one — consistent with the observed ~0.24% failure rate hitting the heavier multimodal archs like InternVLChatModel. Prior art: b6770d7b (#48527) hit OOM in this exact test on ROCm.

### What changed

Added a module-level autouse fixture `cleanup_gpu_memory_between_tests` that runs after each test:

1. `gc.collect()` + `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()`
2. Wait (via NVML, using the existing `wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear` / `wait_for_memory_to_settle` helpers from `tests/utils.py`) for the forked subprocess's VRAM to actually clear before the next test runs. A wait timeout is logged, not raised, so it can never fail a test.

This mirrors the established `clean_gpu_memory_between_tests` fixture in `te

prs.title: [Distributed][MoonEP] BF16 integration of MoonEP balanced EP backend
prs.author: kaijunli-infr
prs.body_head:
## Purpose

First item of the MoonEP integration roadmap RFC #52095: MoonEP (https://github.com/MoonshotAI/MoonEP) as a vLLM all2all backend, BF16 and eager, working end to end with `--all2all-backend moonep`.

MoonEP keeps every EP rank at exactly `S × K` tokens regardless of router skew by planning a few dynamically redundant experts online and prefetching their weights before expert compute. Its contract differs from DeepEP-style backends: `dispatch` returns tokens already grouped per expert row (`[NvS, H]` + `cu_seqlens[E+B]` + an opaque plan), rows `[E, E+B)` are prefetch slots, and there are no per-token top-k ids after dispatch — so the expert compute is a grouped GEMM over `cu_seqlens` segments.

Included:

- `"moonep"` `All2AllBackend`, `has_moonep()`, and `check_moonep_system_support()` (NVSwitch multicast probe run at backend selection so unsupported hosts fail with a clear message)
- `MoonEPAll2AllManager` owning the cached `moonep.Buffer`
- `MoonEPPrepareAndFinalize` on the modular prepare/finalize interface: pad to static capacity → `dispatch` → `prefetch_weight` for the planned redundant experts (plan stashed between prepare and finalize, the same pattern DeepEP-HT uses for its handle) → `combine` in finalize (`TopKWeightAndReduceNoOP`)
- `MoonEPExperts` (`FusedMoEExpertsModular`): three `torch._grouped_mm` calls (gate, up, down) over the `cu_seqlens[E+B]` segments, route weights applied before the down projection; empty segments and unused prefetch slots are skipped natively
- `FusedMoE` wiring: `UnquantizedMoeBackend.MOONEP` (auto-selected when the backend is `moonep`); `convert_to_unquantized_kernel_format` builds the `[E+B]` layout — all-gather each rank's local experts into global order, split into contiguous gate / up / down tensors as MoonEP's prefetch requires — and `_setup_kernel` hands it to the P/F and experts
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_moonep_bf16_poc.py`: multi-GPU test of the full dispatch/prefetch/compute/combine path against the shared

prs.title: [CI] Relax sharded-sampling divergence bound on ROCm
prs.author: khluu
prs.body_head:
## Purpose

`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_sharded_sampling.py::test_sharded_sampling_outputs_match` asserts that batch-sharded sampling matches the replicated fallback up to near-tie boot-state noise, allowing at most `MAX_DIVERGENT_PROMPTS = 3` of 16 prompts to diverge. That bound was tuned on CUDA (measured ≤ 1 divergent prompt per engine boot).

On ROCm/MI300 the engine boots land in noisier kernel/collective states, and the test flakes at **4–7 divergent prompts** — above the CUDA bound but still far below the near-total divergence a real request-misrouting bug produces. In a scan of the last 200 CI builds, this single test accounted for **11 flaky failures**, all on `:amd: (MI300) Distributed DP Basic`, with divergence of 4/16, 5/16, 6/16, and 7/16.

This PR raises the divergence bound to `8` on ROCm only; CUDA keeps the tight bound of `3`. A genuine sharding bug (rows routed to the wrong request, misaligned gathers) still fails, since it diverges on nearly every prompt.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Checked open PRs/issues for `sharded_sampling`, `test_sharded_sampling`, and `prompts diverged`; no existing PR addresses this flake.

## Test plan / commands run

- Flake evidence: analyzed the public Buildkite `ci` pipeline's last 200 builds via the `/data/jobs` endpoint; extracted 240 "failed-then-passed-on-retry" jobs and read each failing attempt's log. 11 were this test, all AMD MI300, divergence 4–7/16 (data and method in the linked tracking issue).
- `pre-commit run` passes (ruff, mypy, etc.) on the changed file.
- This is a numerical-tolerance change to a distributed GPU test; I could not run the full 2-GPU test locally (no multi-GPU box). The ROCm path is exercised by the `:amd: (MI300) Distributed DP Basic` CI job.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code), including the CI log analysis that identified the flake.

prs.title: [Bugfix][Scoring] Warn when serving original Qwen3 reranker without chat template
prs.author: 100milliongold
prs.body_head:
### Purpose
Fixes #55501.

When an original Qwen3 reranker (`Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-*` or `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-*`) is served with `is_original_qwen3_reranker: true` but without `--chat-template`, query and document are concatenated directly without the `<Instruct>/<Query>/<Document>` template wrapper the model was trained with. This causes silent scoring inaccuracy in production environments.

### Changes
- In `CrossEncoderIOProcessor.__init__`, check if `is_original_qwen3_reranker` is enabled and `chat_template` is `None`.
- If so, log a clear startup warning pointing the user to the matching shipped template (`examples/pooling/score/template/qwen3_reranker.jinja` or `examples/pooling/score/template/qwen3_vl_reranker.jinja`).
- Add unit tests in `tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py` verifying the warning behavior for text and vision models, as well as no-warning when a template is passed.

### Test
- Added unit tests covering:
  - `test_qwen3_reranker_warns_without_chat_template`
  - `test_qwen3_vl_reranker_warns_with_vl_template`
  - `test_qwen3_reranker_no_warning_when_template_provided`
- Verified code formatting with `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean.

prs.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Support shared KV prefill in AITER attention
prs.author: AndreasKaratzas
prs.body_head:
- Let AITER attention read K/V from the shared cache when a layer supplies only Q, covering both prefill and chunked prefill.
- Allocate the gather workspace using each attention group's KV dimensions and gather only the new prefill/extend tokens.
- Cover NHD and SHUFFLE layouts, FP8 caches, sliding windows, and cache immutability with 18 regression cases.

`git bisect run` from [nightly 12674](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12674) identified [PR #54917](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54917) as the regression: Gemma stopped computing redundant K/V projections, but AITER still tried to slice those missing tensors. This broke the translation server in build 12711's [MI300](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12711#01a08040-53d9-4f1f-a3f1-004c0a9ac6a4) and [MI355](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12711#01a08040-53f9-493f-9e34-961a3efd1e15) speech jobs. 

This fix was developed with AI assistance and restores the backend's shared-cache support.

prs.title: [Bugfix][Gemma] Conditionally create KV projections/norms on KV-shared layers
prs.author: Josephasafg
prs.body_head:
## Purpose
transformers only creates `k_proj` / `v_proj` / `k_norm` on the **non-KV-shared** layers of Gemma 4 E2B/E4B and Gemma 3n. 
Any checkpoint that goes through `save_pretrained` (HF Trainer, TRL, verl, ...) therefore omits those tensors for the last `num_kv_shared_layers` layers. The original Google releases happen to ship them redundantly, so this only surfaces after fine-tuning.

vLLM created those modules unconditionally, so fine-tuned checkpoints failed with:
```bash
ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: {'...layers.24.self_attn.k_norm.weight', ...}
```
This PR supersedes #41504, has it gone stale and author not responding. 

## Test Plan

CPU unit tests in `tests/models/language/generation/test_gemma.py`:
  - `test_gemma4_kv_shared_layer_loads_plain_q_proj`: shared-layer `q_proj` loads directly, `q/k/v` shards still reach the packed layer, redundant shared-layer K/V names are skipped.
  - `test_gemma3n_kv_shared_layer_mapper`: exact routed names / shard ids for a non-shared and a shared layer.
